en.title: The Elder Scrolls 6 Subtitle 'Sentinel' Finally Revealed Through Starfield Easter Egg
en.summary: After years of speculation, a hidden message within Bethesda's latest RPG, Starfield, appears to have confirmed the long-rumored subtitle for The Elder Scrolls 6. This discovery adds another layer to the anticipation surrounding the next installment in the legendary franchise.
en.body:
The air is thick with anticipation for **The Elder Scrolls 6**, and a recent discovery in **Starfield** has fans buzzing with renewed excitement. For years, players have scoured every official announcement and trailer for clues about the next chapter in Bethesda's iconic RPG series. Now, it seems a definitive answer to the game's subtitle has been hiding in plain sight within the vastness of space.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma recently offered a tantalizing glimpse into **The Elder Scrolls 6**, praising its "scale and grandeur" while cryptically referring to its subtitle using eight asterisks. This deliberate obfuscation sent fans into a frenzy, and a leading contender emerged: **Sentinel**. This name holds significance, being both a prominent city and the capital of a kingdom within the **Elder Scrolls** lore, particularly on the Iliac Bay. This choice would echo the naming conventions of **The Elder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall**, a beloved title for many series veterans. The connection is further strengthened by the rumored development codename for **The Elder Scrolls 6**, which is reportedly **Guardian**—a clear synonym for **Sentinel**.

## A Hidden Message in Starfield

The most compelling evidence, however, comes directly from **Starfield**. A keen-eyed player on Reddit unearthed a sequence within the game's character creation screen: an employee number that, when broken down and translated into letters, spells out S-E-N-T-I-N-E-L. The number sequence, 190514-2009140512, corresponds to the 19th (S), 5th (E), 14th (N), 20th (T), 9th (I), 14th (N), 5th (E), and 12th (L) letters of the alphabet. This intricate Easter egg strongly suggests that **The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel** is indeed the official title. Former Bethesda employee Michael Kirkbride has also reportedly confirmed **Sentinel** as the subtitle, further solidifying this fan theory.

## What This Means for the World

For the passionate **Elder Scrolls** community, this confirmation is monumental. The game is rumored to be set in the provinces of Hammerfell and High Rock, regions rich with history and potential for epic adventures. The inclusion of **Sentinel** as the subtitle hints at a significant narrative focus on this key location, potentially tying into the game's storyline centered around the Adamantine Tower. The prospect of innovative naval and building mechanics, as suggested by some reports, combined with a confirmed setting and title, paints a picture of the most ambitious **Elder Scrolls** title yet. This meticulous layering of hints across Bethesda's titles demonstrates a deep respect for player engagement and lore mastery.

## What's Next

While a release date for **The Elder Scrolls 6** has not yet been officially announced, industry whispers and development progress reports suggest a potential launch around 2028. Players will undoubtedly continue to dissect **Starfield** and any future **Elder Scrolls** content for more hidden clues.

content_raw: While union members outside Bethesda's Maryland office celebrated a recent Microsoft visit by positioning a field of red flags representing laid-off workers and a giant inflatable rat on the lawn , inside the building CEO Asha Sharma was apparently having a delightful time watching a playthrough of The Elder Scrolls 6. So that's nice. "The scale and grandeur are incredible", Sharma said, referring to the game and not the huge blow-up rodent covered in scabs. Sharma was careful to refer to the game's subtitle with a string of asterisks—eight asterisks to be precise, which sent us down a rabbit hole of trying to guess what eight-letter name it could have. Coming in with 14% of the votes in our subsequent poll on the subject was Sentinel, which is the name of a prominent city on the Iliac Bay and also the kingdom it's the capital of. Sentinel is a strong contender because the rumored development codename for The Elder Scrolls 6 is Guardian, a synonym for Sentinel, and naming the game for a city would make for a nice throwback to The Elder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall—which was also named after a city and is still beloved by hardcore fans of the series. (Image credit: Bethesda) It's now an ever stronger contender thanks to an easter egg in Starfield, as unearthed on Reddit . During character creation in Bethesda's sci-fi RPG, your employee number is displayed on the bottom of the screen: 190514-2009140512. Divide those numbers into pairs and you get 19, 05, 14, 20, 09, 14, 05, and 12. The 19th letter of the alphabet is S, the fifth letter is E, the 14th letter is N, and you get the idea. Yep, it spells Sentinel. This might not be the only hint hidden in Starfield. Eagle-eyed watchers noticed a suspicious scratch on a spaceship console in the trailer, and suggested it was shaped like the Iliac Bay , sometimes called Starfall Bay all the way back in the first Elder Scrolls game, Arena. To find any more easter eggs we'd have to go back and replay Starfield, though. Er, you guys have fun with that.
